meta.title: Graph Algorithms: Practical Examples in Apache Spark & Neo4j
meta.author: Mark Needham & Amy E. Hodler

parts.title: Introduction to Graph Analytics and Algorithms

sentences: This book focuses on **graph analytics** – methods to analyze interconnected data such as social networks, **transportation systems**, and **financial markets**.

It explains **graph theory**, a mathematical approach to represent connections, and how **graph algorithms** provide insights by analyzing **nodes** (entities) and **relationships** (connections) between them.
Graphs have evolved from mathematical concepts to practical tools in analyzing complex, real-world interconnected data.

Furthermore, it provides practical examples using **Apache Spark** and **Neo4j** platforms, making it applicable for **developers** and **data scientists** seeking to leverage graph data more effectively.
**Graph algorithms** provide mathematical solutions to understand **complex networks** by analyzing **connections in data**.
These are pivotal in fields such as **network science**, which uses them to **predict behavior** or **uncover hidden patterns** like **fraud** or **congestion**.
For example, they helped analyze **US airport network delays** by identifying **systematic issues**.
**Graph processing** involves specific **graph workloads** that are important for **performing real-time transactions** or **pattern queries** using graph databases.
Meanwhile, **graph algorithms** focus on the **entire graph** to determine **global patterns**, helping organizations **model systems** or predict outcomes based on **network dynamics**.

This convergence of **transaction processing with analytics** represents a merging known as **HTAP** (Hybrid Transactional/Analytical Processing), enabling **real-time decisions** with **integrated analytics**.

parts.title: Bipartite to Monopartite Graphs and Graph Algorithms Overview

sentences: **Bipartite graphs** are often transformed into **monopartite graphs** for more in-depth analysis.
Understanding the three main areas of graph **algorithms** is fundamental: **pathfinding**, **centrality computation**, and **community detection**.
In **pathfinding**, algorithms help uncover **shortest paths**—the route with the fewest hops or lowest weight—between nodes.
This is key for analyzing network **efficiency** and **resiliency**.
**Centrality** algorithms assess which nodes are crucial for **information spread** or linking **distinct groups**.
For **community detection**, **connectedness** helps identify **substructures** in networks that emerge naturally, such as hubs or **hierarchies**.
Pathfinding in graphs dates back to the 19th century but became notable in the 1950s.
The most famed algorithm for this is **Dijkstra's Shortest Path**.
**Dijkstra** starts by finding the lowest-weight link from the starting node, then "waves" through the graph, computing cumulative weights to determine the shortest path to the destination node.
When discussing paths, terms like **weight**, **cost**, **distance**, and **hops** are key.
Weight is the numeric value of a link, while distance often measures the cost of traversal, which isn't always physical distance.
When to use **Shortest Path**?
For finding optimal routes between two nodes, like on Google Maps for driving directions, or determining social network connectivity degrees.

parts.title: Algorithms for Exploring Connections and Influences in Graphs

sentences: The Minimum Spanning Tree algorithm finds the shortest path connecting all nodes starting from **Amsterdam**.
The **relationship cost** used is indicated by **distance**.
It identifies critical paths like **Amsterdam to Utrecht** as having the least connection costened within the graph.
The **Random Walk algorithm** is a way of creating a path through a graph by random selection of nodes, starting from **London**.
This helps in highlighting how nodes are interrelated in a **random manner** which has practical applications in generating node embeddings and community detection.
In large **graphs**, completely calculating **centrality** can be challenging because of runtime concerns.
For this reason, it's recommended to first simplify to a **subgraph**, or use an approximation algorithm such as **RA-Brandes**, which can handle only a subset of **nodes** efficiently.

Adding a **user** like Jason connects **disparate groups** and raises his **centrality** significantly, acting as a **bridge** between clusters, though this will change the network's **structure** and its paths.
When **calculating** betweenness and centrality metrics, it is important to remember that the measurements gained are relative and don't quantify real-world impact directly.
**PageRank**, on the other hand, evaluates not the number of **connections** but the quality by tracing **links** and examining their **weight** or importance.
It reflects broader network **influence**, offering alternative insights beyond direct node influence.

Despite its **originality** in ranking web pages, **PageRank** has grown versatile, now enhancing fields like **follower recommendations** or **fraud detection** by considering how **nodes influence** others through their interconnections.
As nodes reach equilibrium within the **PageRank formula**, it highlights more influential **nodes** while avoiding **rank sinks** by distributing rank due to **dangling nodes**.

Practitioners must explore the graph **structure** to gain meaningful results from **PageRank** and understand factors like possible **rank sinks** or node **degeneracy** when unexpected results arise.

Furthermore, **Personalized PageRank** offers specificity by focusing on targeted nodes, signifying its importance in recommendation systems where **specific relationships** have measurable influence.

parts.title: Applying Graph Algorithms to Large Datasets

sentences: Large datasets are analyzed using graph algorithms, specifically through the lens of **Yelp** and **US Department of Transportation** data.
We demonstrate the application of various algorithms like **PageRank** for identifying influential Yelp reviewers, and **Betweenness Centrality** to connect reviewers across groups.
The utility of **Label Propagation** for clustering similar Yelp businesses into categories, and **Degree Centrality** for recognizing airport hubs in transportation data is highlighted.
Furthermore, **Connected Components** are applied to cluster airport routes.
The discussed graph algorithms help in understanding network structures and inform strategic business insights.
GraphFrames is used to analyze flight delays and routes.
Patterns or subgraphs, known as motifs, can identify delayed flights, such as those at **San Francisco International Airport** (SFO).
Motifs allow us to detect flights with interconnected delays on different legs of the journey.
Interestingly, flights to **North Central West Virginia Airport** (**CKB**) from **Chicago O'Hare International Airport** (**ORD**) show significant delays, skewing the average.
Analyzing delays upon arrival and departure at SFO, motifs reveal that some flights are delayed but manage to reduce delays while on the ground.

Understanding **delays**, patterns, and airline networks can help optimize travel plans and maximize frequent flyer points utilization by figuring out who's flying where and when delays typically happen.

parts.title: Graph-Based Link Prediction in Collaboration Networks

sentences: We explored the use of graph algorithms to predict future links between authors using the **Citation Network Dataset**.
Initially, **COAUTHOREARLY** and **COAUTHORLATE** relationships were created based on collaboration timelines, with **2006** as the dividing year.
This split facilitated a **balanced training and test dataset** with equal numbers of positive (collaborative pairs) and negative examples (non-collaborative pairs).
To make predictions, we focused on features like **common authors** and **preferential attachment**.
Using Neo4j's **Cypher queries**, these features were calculated as they are indicative of future collaborations.
A **Random Forest model** in Spark was trained using these features as part of the **machine learning pipeline**.
The model's effectiveness was evaluated using metrics such as **accuracy, precision, recall**, and a plot of **ROC curves**.

paragraphs.heading: Summary of Key Concepts:
sentences: Various **graph algorithms** like **Centrality** and **Community Detection** have applications within machine learning and data analysis.
Techniques such as **feature extraction** and tools like **Apache Spark** and **Neo4j** enhance predictions by analyzing complex data structures.
Experiments showcase implementing these algorithms for **link prediction**, improving accuracy by incorporating features like **Triangles and Clustering Coefficient**, and community insights.
